tagline: All the way around the Presidentials, through both notches.
intro: From Littleton the loop goes up NH 116 to Whitefield and US 3 to Lancaster, then turns east on US 2 through Jefferson and Randolph, where the whole of the Presidential Range comes into view. NH 16 takes it south through Pinkham Notch to Jackson, and US 302 brings it back west through Bartlett, up Crawford Notch and past Bretton Woods and Bethlehem to Littleton.

These were grand-hotel towns. Bethlehem once had over 30 hotels and seven trains a day, many of the guests there for the low pollen count. In Crawford Notch, in 1826, the Willey family left their house for shelter in a storm and died in the rockslide. The house was untouched.

moments.title: Mount Washington Cog Railway
moments.text: On a clear day the Cog's smoke shows on Mount Washington's western slope from Route 2, the world's first mountain-climbing cog railway and once mocked as a railway to the moon.

moments.title: Pinkham Notch
moments.text: Route 16 runs up a glacier-cut valley with Mount Washington rising more than 4,000 feet above the floor on one side and the Wildcat Range on the other.

moments.title: Mount Washington Hotel
moments.text: At the 1902 opening Joseph Stickney called himself the poor fool who built all this, and in 1944 his hotel hosted the conference that set up the World Bank.
